source: Hand-written by the Interim team from CLAUDE.md §3.4/§8 and CONTRACTS.md §1/§6. Expected outputs were derived by hand from the rule tables (see each persona's `derivation`) and then verified against the rules engine by packages/rules/tests/test_personas.py. Clinical stories are invented for synthetic participants on a cemiplimab (PD-1 inhibitor) study; nothing here is real patient data.
rationale: Deterministic answer key for the eval harness (scripts/run_eval.py -> docs/eval/results.md). The mix covers every rung of the escalation ladder, every red flag, every corroboration rule, every con-med match kind, every vitals quality status and the de-duplication window from both sides, so that precision/recall per tier and per grade are computed over a set where the correct answer is known. The five hidden judge personas are meant to be run live from the Eval page; the `counterfactuals` on three personas encode 'change one input, watch the output change'.

persona.id: Stable kebab-case id prefixed T0-/T1-/T2-/T3-/E-/J-/P3- by category.
persona.category: tier0 | tier1 | tier2 | tier3 | edge | judge | protocol (judge personas are hidden: true; protocol personas, added with CONTRACTS.md R3.1, exercise the EMPOWER-Lung 1 protocol rules: possible AESI, con-med levels, CM missing fields).
persona.protocol_context: Optional (protocol personas): {prior_pi3k_inhibitor, last_dose_date} passed to the engine as CheckInInput.protocol_context; absent means no prior PI3K inhibitor and last dose unknown.
persona.consent_camera: false means no vitals_samples at all (camera declined).
persona.vitals_scenario: Closest mock scenario (resting, tachypnea, post_exercise, low_quality) or custom / none; informational, the explicit vitals_samples are what the runner replays.
persona.settings: RuleSettings overrides for the main check-in; simulated_as_measured is the admin demo toggle.
persona.setup.prior_checkins: Replayed before the main check-in as the same participant, days_ago earlier, with their AE drafts confirmed so they become open AEs for de-duplication.
persona.responses: {item_id: {attribute: int}} for all ten items with every attribute explicit.
persona.gates: hospitalization, conmed_changed, conmed_text (verbatim), conmed_direction, other_text (verbatim), optional temp_c.
persona.vitals_samples: Bridge-shaped camelCase samples; tsOffsetS is seconds after session start. One sample every 2 s from t = 20 s: pulse only (windowS 12) before t = 30 s, pulse + breathing (windowS 30) from t = 30 s, HRV from t = 60 s where present.
persona.counterfactuals: Optional: the same persona re-run with different settings and a partial expected block.
persona.derivation: The hand derivation of `expected` from the rule tables.

expected.grades: Provisional CTCAE grade per item (all ten).
expected.red_flag_tier_floor: Highest tier_floor among fired red flags (0 when none).
expected.rules_fired_includes: Rule ids that must appear in rules_fired.
expected.rules_fired_excludes: Rule ids that must NOT appear in rules_fired.
expected.sae_clock_started: true iff hospitalization = yes; due_at = completed_at + 24 h.
expected.seriousness_suspected: Same trigger as the SAE clock.
expected.ae_drafts: Number of AE drafts including follow-ups.
expected.vs_drafts: Number of VS summary rows (0 without samples; PULSE + RESP; + HRV_RMSSD when any sample carries HRV).
expected.vs_not_done: Optional: VSTESTCD codes whose row has VSSTAT = NOT DONE.
expected.cm: CM drafts in order: {verbatim, cmdecod, min_confidence, match_kind?, distance?, direction?}.
expected.dedup_followups: Number of AE drafts linked to an open AE as follow-ups.
expected.vitals_status: VitalsAssessment.status: ok | unavailable | low_quality | implausible | simulated_ignored.
expected.protocol_tier_floor: Optional: CheckInResult.protocol_tier_floor (2 for a prohibited con-med, else 0).
expected.aesi_suspected: Optional: ProtocolAssessment.aesi_suspected (possible AESI, investigator to confirm).
expected.aesi_clock_started: Optional: an AESI clock (kind aesi) started; due_at = completed_at + 24 h.
expected.aesi_items: Optional: ProtocolAssessment.aesi_items in instrument order; these AE drafts carry INTERIM_AESI_SUSPECTED = true.
expected.cm[].protocol_flag / cm[].missing_fields: Optional: INTERIM_PROTOCOL_FLAG (prohibited | discouraged | permitted | null) and INTERIM_CM_MISSING_FIELDS of the CM draft.

schema.replay_conventions: Each persona is its own synthetic participant (so open AEs never leak between personas). The runner chooses completed_at ('now'), sets started_at = completed_at - session length, materializes tsUtc = started_at + tsOffsetS, and gives every answer ts = completed_at.

personas.name: No symptoms, resting vitals
personas.description: Every item answered None / Never / No. Nothing to grade; only VS rows drafted.
personas.story: Week-3 between-visit check-in on cemiplimab. The participant feels well and reports nothing.
personas.derivation: Every zero-gate attribute is 0, so every composite is 0 and no score/grade rule is emitted; max grade 0 -> base tier 0. No gate is yes and no text is given, so no red flag fires. Vitals are SIMULATED with the demo toggle OFF -> status simulated_ignored (summarized for the record, not eligible for corroboration). Final tier 0 (Log). Drafts: no AE, no CM, two VS summary rows (PULSE, RESP) with VSMETHOD = Simulated.

personas.name: Mild fatigue and cough, started Tylenol PM
personas.description: Two G1 items; multi-word brand-name con-med resolved through its first token.
personas.story: A little tired and a tickly cough after a cold. Started taking Tylenol PM at night to sleep.
personas.derivation: fatigue sev 1 / int 1 -> two_attribute_sev_int row (1,1) = composite 1 -> G1; cough sev 1 / int 0 -> row (1,0) = composite 1 -> G1. Max grade 1 -> base tier 0; no red flag; simulated vitals ignored -> tier 0. Con-med: the whole string 'Tylenol PM' is not in the list and is > 2 edits from any entry, so the matcher tries tokens of >= 4 characters; 'Tylenol' lower-cases to the brand entry 'tylenol' -> case-insensitive match, normalized to its generic acetaminophen, confidence 1.0 ('PM' is too short to be tried alone). Two AE drafts (Fatigue G1, Cough G1), one CM draft with CMSTDTC set and CMENDTC null.

personas.name: Declined camera, mild joint pain
personas.description: consent_camera = false: no vitals at all. The check-in must work exactly the same.
personas.story: Sore knees after gardening; a little bit of trouble on stairs. Preferred not to use the camera.
personas.derivation: joint_pain sev 1 / int 2 -> sev_int row (1,2) = composite 1 -> G1 -> base tier 0. No samples were captured (camera declined) -> vitals.unavailable, status unavailable, no VS rows and no corroboration possible. Tier 0. One AE draft (Arthralgia G1).

personas.name: Occasional mild nausea with a free-text comment
personas.description: Free text is present but no item is severe, so the other_text red flag must NOT fire.
personas.story: Queasy a couple of mornings. Mentions poor sleep in the comment box.

gates.other_text: I have been sleeping badly since the last visit, maybe that is why I feel off.

personas.derivation: nausea freq 2 / sev 1 -> two_attribute_freq_sev row (2,1) = composite 1 -> G1 -> base tier 0. redflag.other_text_with_severe needs BOTH a non-empty comment AND a severe item (severity >= 3); nausea severity is 1, so it does not fire and the comment is simply stored verbatim for a human to read. Tier 0. One AE draft (Nausea G1); no CM draft because conmed_changed is false.

personas.name: Rash present, mild itching, finished an amoxicillin course
personas.description: Presence item and single-attribute item at G1; con-med direction 'both' (started and stopped).
personas.story: A faint rash on the forearms with mild itch. Took a 7-day course of amoxicillin for a dental infection; finished it.
personas.derivation: rash presence 1 -> composite 1 (Interim presence convention) -> G1; itching sev 1 -> single_attribute severity 1 -> composite 1 -> G1. Max grade 1 -> tier 0; no red flag. Con-med 'amoxicillin' is an exact entry -> confidence 1.0; direction 'both' sets CMSTDTC and CMENDTC to the check-in date. Two AE drafts (Rash maculo-papular G1, Pruritus G1), one CM draft.

personas.name: Occasional diarrhea, prior AE 12 days ago, long capture with HRV
personas.description: A prior open AE for the same term is OUTSIDE the 7-day window -> new AE, not a follow-up. Capture ran past 60 s so an HRV row is drafted.
personas.story: Loose stools a few times this week, as in the check-in two weeks ago. Sat still through a long capture.

prior_checkins.note: Creates an open Diarrhea AE (G1) 12 days before the main check-in: outside the 7-day window.

personas.derivation: diarrhea freq 2 -> single_attribute frequency 2 -> composite 1 -> G1 -> tier 0. The prior check-in (12 days ago) left an open Diarrhea AE whose last report is 12 days before this one; the dedup window is 7 days inclusive, so dedup.new_ae fires and a NEW AE draft is created (dedup_followups 0). VS: PULSE, RESP and, because samples from t = 60 s carry hrvRmssdMs with windowS 60 (the HRV averaging window; the engine ignores an HRV reading whose window is shorter than 60 s), an HRV_RMSSD row with a value -> 3 VS drafts, none NOT DONE.
personas.vitals_note: 22 samples, t = 20..62 s: pulse only before 30 s, pulse + breathing from 30 s, HRV (RMSSD) from 60 s.

personas.name: Moderate shortness of breath, started loratadine
personas.description: The demo persona. One G2 item, one G1 item, con-med exact match.
personas.story: P-007's first demo check-in: moderate breathlessness that somewhat interferes with daily activities, a mild cough, started loratadine for allergies.
personas.derivation: shortness_of_breath sev 2 / int 2 -> sev_int row (2,2) = composite 2 -> G2; cough (1,0) -> composite 1 -> G1. Max grade 2 -> base tier 1. No red flag (severity 2 < 3, no hospitalization). Vitals are simulated and the toggle is OFF -> simulated_ignored, so even a tachypneic reading could not bump the tier. Final tier 1 (Coordinator review within 1 business day). Con-med 'loratadine' exact -> 1.0. Drafts: AE Dyspnea G2, AE Cough G1, VS PULSE + RESP (Simulated), CM loratadine. Identical to CONTRACTS.md §6.

personas.name: Moderate fatigue, started Claritin
personas.description: Single G2 on fatigue; brand-name con-med with a capital letter resolves case-insensitively to its generic.
personas.story: Tired most afternoons and cutting errands short. Started Claritin for hay fever.
personas.derivation: fatigue sev 2 / int 2 -> composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1; nothing else reported; no red flag; simulated vitals ignored -> tier 1. 'Claritin' is not an exact entry (names are lowercase) but 'claritin' is a brand entry whose generic is loratadine -> case_insensitive, confidence 1.0, CMDECOD = loratadine while CMTRT keeps 'Claritin' verbatim.

personas.name: Moderate nausea, started 'ondansatrone' (misspelled)
personas.description: Single G2 on nausea; con-med misspelled by two edits matches through Levenshtein at the distance boundary.
personas.story: Nauseous most days, moderate at worst. Started the anti-sickness tablets the clinic gave her and typed the name from memory.
personas.derivation: nausea freq 3 / sev 2 -> freq_sev row (3,2) = composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1 -> tier 1. 'ondansatrone' vs 'ondansetron': substitute e->a and append e = Levenshtein distance 2, exactly the table maximum; confidence = round(1 - 2 / max(12, 11), 2) = 0.83. CMDECOD = ondansetron, CMTRT verbatim 'ondansatrone'.

personas.name: Moderate joint pain that gets in the way quite a bit
personas.description: Single G2 on joint pain driven by interference; no con-med.
personas.story: Stiff, aching hands and knees in the morning; quite a bit of trouble with buttons and stairs.
personas.derivation: joint_pain sev 2 / int 3 -> sev_int row (2,3) = composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1 -> tier 1. No gates answered yes; no con-med. One AE draft (Arthralgia G2).

personas.name: Moderate mouth sores, mild fatigue, unmatched con-med
personas.description: G2 on mouth sores plus a G1; the con-med text matches nothing and is kept verbatim for the coordinator.
personas.story: Painful sores inside the cheeks make eating uncomfortable. Started a herbal remedy a relative recommended.
personas.derivation: mouth_sores sev 2 / int 2 -> composite 2 -> G2; fatigue (1,1) -> composite 1 -> G1. Max grade 2 -> tier 1. Neither the whole string nor either token ('elderberry', 'gummies') is within 2 edits of any bundled name -> conmed.unmatched, CMDECOD null, confidence 0.0, CMTRT verbatim, flagged for the coordinator. Two AE drafts, one CM draft.

personas.name: Moderate shortness of breath with tachypneic SIMULATED vitals, toggle OFF
personas.description: Counterpart of T2-dyspnea-tachypnea-corroborated: the same answers and the same breathing rate, but the vitals are simulated and the demo toggle is OFF, so they cannot bump the tier.
personas.story: The demo's first check-in repeated with the mock in its 'tachypnea' scenario while the admin toggle is still off.
personas.derivation: Same grades as T1-dyspnea-moderate (Dyspnea G2, Cough G1) -> base tier 1. Breathing 26-27 breaths/min would satisfy corr.tachypnea_dyspnea (>= 24), but every sample is isMeasured = false and simulated_as_measured is OFF, so no reading is corroboration-eligible: status simulated_ignored, corroboration not evaluated, tier stays 1. The VS rows still record breathing 26 (Simulated).

personas.name: Severe fatigue (G3) with no red flag
personas.description: A provisional G3 alone sets tier 2. Severe item present but no fever and no comment, so no red flag.
personas.story: Exhausted; spends most of the day on the sofa and has stopped driving.
personas.derivation: fatigue sev 3 / int 3 -> sev_int row (3,3) = composite 3 -> G3 -> base tier 2. Fatigue severity 3 is a 'severe item', but redflag.fever_with_severe also needs fever present and redflag.other_text_with_severe needs a comment; neither is given, so no floor applies. Simulated vitals ignored. Final tier 2 (Nurse call today), no stop screen.

personas.name: Fever with severe joint pain (red flag), started acetaminophen
personas.description: Red flag fever_with_severe floors the tier at 2 even though the highest provisional grade is only 2 (base tier 1).
personas.story: Chills and a 38.4 C reading two nights ago; joints so painful she rates them severe. Started acetaminophen.
personas.derivation: joint_pain sev 3 / int 2 -> sev_int row (3,2) = composite 2 -> G2; fever presence 1 -> composite 1 -> G1. Max grade 2 -> base tier 1. Red flag fever_with_severe: fever present AND joint_pain severity 3 >= 3 -> tier floor 2 > base 1 -> tier.redflag_floor raises tier to 2. Pulse ~88 is below the 110 tachycardia threshold and the toggle is OFF anyway, so corr.tachycardia_fever cannot fire. The typed temperature 38.4 is attached as evidence only. Two AE drafts (Arthralgia G2, Fever G1), one CM.

personas.name: Severe mouth sores with a free-text comment (red flag)
personas.description: Comment present AND a severe item -> other_text_with_severe floors the tier at 2 and flags the text for a human read.
personas.story: Sores are severe at their worst and get in the way somewhat; writes that swallowing hurts and meals are being skipped.

gates.other_text: The sores make it hard to swallow and I have been skipping meals.

personas.derivation: mouth_sores sev 3 / int 2 -> sev_int row (3,2) = composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1. Red flag other_text_with_severe: other_text non-empty AND mouth_sores severity 3 >= 3 -> floor 2 -> tier 2. The text is never parsed; it only raises the flag. One AE draft (Mucositis oral G2).

personas.name: Moderate shortness of breath + tachypnea, toggle ON (demo second check-in)
personas.description: The demo's second check-in: identical answers to T1-dyspnea-moderate, breathing 26 with 'treat simulated as measured' ON. Grade unchanged, tier +1.
personas.story: P-007 repeats the check-in after the admin switches the mock to 'tachypnea' (later: after jumping jacks in front of a real sensor).
personas.derivation: Grades identical to the demo persona: Dyspnea G2, Cough G1 -> base tier 1; no red flag. With the toggle ON every confident, plausible simulated reading is corroboration-eligible (vitals.simulated_as_measured warning fires; status ok). Max eligible breathing = 27 >= 24 and shortness_of_breath composite 2 >= 2 -> corr.tachypnea_dyspnea ('tachypnea corroborates reported dyspnea') -> +1 -> tier 2. Max pulse 100 < 110 so corr.tachycardia_dyspnea does not fire. AETOXGR stays 2: vitals never change a grade.

counterfactuals.label: same inputs with the demo toggle OFF

personas.name: G3 shortness of breath with low-quality vitals: no bump, no stop screen
personas.description: Base tier 2 from a G3; the camera readings would corroborate but none reaches the confidence threshold, so the tier does NOT become 3.
personas.story: Breathless enough that daily activities are very much affected (moderate at worst, but constant interference). Poor lighting; the camera never locked onto the face.
personas.derivation: shortness_of_breath sev 2 / int 4 -> sev_int row (2,4) = composite 3 -> G3 -> base tier 2. Severity is 2 (< 3) so redflag.severe_dyspnea does not fire. Every sample confidence is below min_confidence 0.6 -> every reading is low_confidence -> vitals.low_quality, status low_quality, no summary, both VS rows NOT DONE, corroboration not evaluated (the toggle is ON but there is nothing eligible). Tier stays 2: had the readings been trustworthy, tier 2 + corroboration would have been tier 3 and a stop screen.

personas.name: ER visit since last visit with only mild nausea: SAE clock starts
personas.description: Hospitalization/ER = yes is a red flag with floor 3 and a seriousness trigger even when the symptoms are mild.
personas.story: Went to the ER on Tuesday for vomiting and dehydration, was rehydrated and sent home. Feels mostly fine now.

gates.other_text: I went to the ER on Tuesday because I could not keep fluids down.

personas.derivation: nausea freq 1 / sev 1 -> freq_sev row (1,1) = composite 1 -> G1 -> base tier 0. Red flag hospitalization (gate = yes) -> floor 3 and seriousness -> tier 3 (Urgent): stop screen shown, on-call paged. seriousness_suspected = true (ICH E2A hospitalization criterion); the SAE clock starts at completed_at with investigator-to-sponsor due 24 h later. The comment is present but no item is severe, so other_text_with_severe does not fire. One AE draft (Nausea G1) with INTERIM_TIER 3.

personas.name: Severe shortness of breath (red flag), no hospitalization
personas.description: Severe dyspnea is itself an urgent red flag: floor 3 with no seriousness trigger and no SAE clock.
personas.story: Breathless walking across the room; moderate cough. Has not been to a hospital.
personas.derivation: shortness_of_breath sev 3 / int 3 -> composite 3 -> G3 -> base tier 2; cough sev 2 / int 1 -> row (2,1) = composite 1 -> G1. Red flag severe_dyspnea (severity 3 >= 3) -> floor 3 > base 2 -> tier 3: stop screen, page. No hospitalization -> seriousness not suspected, no SAE clock. Two AE drafts.

personas.name: Very severe shortness of breath and a hospital admission
personas.description: Two tier-3 red flags at once; seriousness suspected and the SAE clock starts.
personas.story: Admitted overnight for breathing difficulty; discharged yesterday; still very short of breath.
personas.derivation: shortness_of_breath sev 4 / int 4 -> composite 3 -> G3 (grade 4 is never assigned by software) -> base tier 2. Red flags severe_dyspnea (floor 3) and hospitalization (floor 3, seriousness) -> tier 3, stop screen, page, seriousness_suspected, SAE clock due +24 h. One AE draft (Dyspnea G3).

personas.name: G3 shortness of breath + tachycardia, toggle ON: tier 2 becomes tier 3
personas.description: The ladder's 'Tier 2 plus a corroboration rule -> Tier 3' step, reached without any red flag.
personas.story: Moderate breathlessness that very much limits activity; the camera shows a resting pulse in the mid-110s.
personas.derivation: shortness_of_breath sev 2 / int 4 -> composite 3 -> G3 -> base tier 2; severity 2 < 3 so no severe_dyspnea red flag. Toggle ON -> eligible; max pulse 115 >= 110 with composite 3 >= 2 -> corr.tachycardia_dyspnea -> +1 -> min(3, 2 + 1) = 3: stop screen and page. Breathing max 17 < 24 so tachypnea does not fire. No hospitalization -> no SAE clock. Grade stays 3.
personas.vitals_note: Steady pulse 112-115 with normal breathing 16-17: resembles the tail of the mock 'post_exercise' scenario.

counterfactuals.label: same inputs with the demo toggle OFF

personas.name: Breathing rate 50 (implausible) with moderate dyspnea, toggle ON
personas.description: A breathing value outside 5-45 is flagged implausible and ignored for rules even with the toggle ON; the RESP row is NOT DONE and the tier stays 1.
personas.story: Moderate breathlessness; the mock emits a nonsense breathing rate of ~50 while the pulse is fine.
personas.derivation: Dyspnea composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1. Breathing 50-53 breaths/min is above the plausibility maximum 45 -> each such sample fires vitals.implausible and its breathing is ignored for rules; pulse 74 is usable and (toggle ON) eligible, so status is ok and corroboration IS evaluated: no eligible breathing maximum exists -> corr.tachypnea_dyspnea cannot match; pulse 76 < 110. Tier stays 1. VS: PULSE drafted with a value, RESP drafted with VSSTAT = NOT DONE.
personas.vitals_note: Pulse ~74 (plausible); breathing 50-53 (> 45, implausible) on every sample that carries breathing.

personas.name: Corroborating values at confidence 0.3 everywhere: ignored
personas.description: Pulse 112 and breathing 27 would fire two corroboration rules, but every confidence is 0.3 (< 0.6), so the whole session is low_quality and the tier is unchanged.
personas.story: Moderate breathlessness; the participant kept talking and moving, so every reading came back with confidence 0.3.
personas.derivation: Dyspnea composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1. Confidence 0.3 < min_confidence 0.6 on every metric of every sample -> all readings low_confidence -> vitals.low_quality, status low_quality, no summary, no eligible readings, so neither corr.tachypnea_dyspnea (breathing 27) nor corr.tachycardia_dyspnea (pulse 112) can fire despite the toggle being ON. Tier 1 unchanged; both VS rows NOT DONE.

personas.name: Cough again three days after an open cough AE: follow-up, not a new AE
personas.description: A prior check-in 3 days ago opened a Cough AE; today's cough links to it (AESTDTC kept) while today's new fatigue opens a new AE.
personas.story: Still coughing, a bit more disruptive than three days ago, and now a little tired too.

prior_checkins.note: Opens a Cough AE (G1) 3 days before the main check-in: inside the 7-day window.

personas.derivation: cough sev 1 / int 1 -> composite 1 -> G1; fatigue (1,0) -> G1 -> tier 0. The prior check-in opened AE 'Cough' last reported 3.0 days ago, inside the 7-day inclusive window -> dedup.followup_linked: today's Cough draft is a follow-up (is_followup, INTERIM_FOLLOWUP_OF set, AESTDTC = the prior first report, AEONGO = Y) and counts toward ae_drafts. Fatigue has no open AE -> dedup.new_ae. ae_drafts 2, dedup_followups 1.

personas.name: Post-exercise pulse 190: implausible, ignored even with the toggle ON
personas.description: Judge persona. A pulse above 180 is sensor nonsense by the plausibility table and never reaches the corroboration rules.
personas.story: Moderate breathlessness reported right after running up the stairs to the kiosk; the mock reports a pulse of 181-190.
personas.derivation: Dyspnea composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1. Every pulse value is above the plausibility maximum 180 -> vitals.implausible per sample and no usable pulse at all (PULSE row NOT DONE). Breathing 18-20 is usable and eligible (toggle ON) -> status ok, corroboration evaluated: no eligible pulse maximum, breathing max 20 < 24 -> nothing fires. Tier 1. Had the pulse been a plausible 150 it would have fired corr.tachycardia_dyspnea and bumped to tier 2; 190 is excluded precisely because a camera cannot be trusted there.
personas.vitals_note: Pulse 190 decaying to 181 (all > 180, implausible); breathing 18-20 (plausible, below the 24 threshold).

personas.name: Only the toggle matters: moderate dyspnea with pulse 112-115
personas.description: Judge persona. With the demo toggle OFF these exact inputs are tier 1; with it ON the tachycardia rule bumps them to tier 2. Encoded with the toggle ON; the counterfactual encodes OFF.
personas.story: Moderate breathlessness; the camera reports a steady pulse of 112-115 and normal breathing.
personas.derivation: Dyspnea composite 2 -> G2 -> base tier 1; no red flag. Toggle ON: max eligible pulse 115 >= 110 with composite 2 >= 2 -> corr.tachycardia_dyspnea -> tier 2. Toggle OFF (counterfactual): the same samples are simulated_ignored, corroboration is not evaluated, tier 1. Grades, drafts and everything else are identical in both runs; only the escalation tier differs.

counterfactuals.label: same inputs with the demo toggle OFF

personas.name: Stopped prednisone; itching back to moderate, rash present
personas.description: Judge persona. Con-med direction 'stopped': CMENDTC is set and CMSTDTC is null.
personas.story: Finished the steroid taper for the rash last week; the itch is back and moderate.
personas.derivation: itching sev 2 -> single_attribute severity 2 -> composite 2 -> G2; rash presence 1 -> G1. Max grade 2 -> tier 1. 'prednisone' is an exact entry (nearest other: prednisolone at distance 2, but exact wins) -> confidence 1.0. Direction 'stopped' -> CMENDTC = check-in date, CMSTDTC null, INTERIM_DIRECTION stopped. Two AE drafts, one CM draft.

personas.name: Fever with pulse 115 (toggle ON) and moderate fatigue
personas.description: Judge persona. corr.tachycardia_fever bumps a base tier 1 to tier 2; no severe item, so the fever red flag does not fire.
personas.story: Chills overnight and a 38.1 C reading; moderately tired. The camera shows a pulse in the mid-110s.
personas.derivation: fatigue sev 2 / int 2 -> composite 2 -> G2; fever presence 1 -> G1. Max grade 2 -> base tier 1. redflag.fever_with_severe needs a severe item (severity >= 3): fatigue is 2, so it does not fire. Toggle ON: max eligible pulse 117 >= 110 with fever present -> corr.tachycardia_fever ('tachycardia with reported fever or chills') -> +1 -> tier 2. Dyspnea composite is 0 so the dyspnea rules cannot match. Two AE drafts (Fatigue G2, Fever G1 with the typed temperature as evidence).

personas.name: Every item at its maximum, no hospitalization
personas.description: Judge persona. All ten items at their worst answer: tier 3 via the severe-dyspnea red flag, but no SAE clock because there was no hospitalization.
personas.story: A stress test: Very severe / Very much / Almost constantly / Yes on every screen; answered No to the hospital question.
personas.derivation: Two-attribute rows (4,4) = composite 3 for shortness of breath, cough, fatigue, nausea, joint pain and mouth sores; diarrhea frequency 4 -> 3; itching severity 4 -> 3 (capped); rash and fever presence -> 1. Max grade 3 -> base tier 2. Red flags: severe_dyspnea (severity 4 >= 3) -> floor 3; fever_with_severe (fever present + severe items) -> floor 2; hospitalization = no and other_text empty -> those two do not fire. Floor 3 -> tier 3, stop screen, page; seriousness NOT suspected and no SAE clock because only the hospital gate starts it. Grade 4 is never assigned. Ten AE drafts.

personas.name: Severe itching with a rash: possible AESI, 24-hour clock
personas.description: Itching Severe (G3) plus a rash. Tier 2 from the grade; the protocol makes a grade 3 skin AE a possible AESI, so a 24-hour AESI clock starts. No SAE clock.
personas.story: Week 6 on cemiplimab. The participant reports a rash and itching bad enough to keep them up at night. EMPOWER-Lung 1 §9.4.3 (p. 92) lists 'Grade 3 or greater irAEs' as adverse events of special interest, reportable within 24 hours like an SAE. The kiosk asks rash only as present/absent (at most grade 1), so the grade 3 skin AE a kiosk can show is itching (pruritus).
personas.derivation: itching severity 3 -> single_attribute severity 3 -> composite 3 -> G3; rash presence 1 -> G1 (presence convention).
